title: Chapter 259: Three Taboos Inside the Haunted House [2 in 1]
html:
“Boss, your Haunted House is impressive.” Noticing Chen Ge watching him, the man smiled politely and added, “I was a timid child, so the neighborhood kids often bullied me. My older brother brought me here to build my courage, but I ended up falling in love with the excitement.”

“Then you’ll certainly enjoy the next scenario.” The man’s behavior struck Chen Ge as odd. Without being asked a single question, he had volunteered an entire explanation. Is he nervous?

Chen Ge gave no sign of suspicion. He kept smiling, presenting the visitors with a friendly, considerate host.

“All right, it’s time to enter.” Chen Ge led the way and drew back the curtains that shut out the sunlight. Inside the Haunted House, he presented the seven visitors with liability waivers. “Two-star scenarios are different from one-star scenarios. Before beginning the challenge, each of you must sign one of these.”

He laid the forms on the table. Three visitors signed without hesitation, while two others picked theirs up and read every line.

“Do we really need to sign this?” The seventh visitor—the man Chen Ge had recognized—hesitated visibly. His gaze flicked toward another member of the group.

He has a partner?

Chen Ge pretended not to notice. “Of course. Visitors normally sign waivers for our one-star scenarios as well, but today’s crowds forced us to adjust the rules at the last minute.”

“Okay then.”

Chen Ge watched the group closely, allowing no movement to escape his attention. This major promotion marked a new beginning for the Haunted House. He would permit neither mistakes nor accidents to spoil it.

The visitors began signing. The ordinary-looking man called himself Wei Wu; the visitor with whom he had exchanged a glance was Kong Xiangming. Unlike the others, neither showed excitement nor nervousness, and both kept an unusually low profile.

The other five seemed far more ordinary. Three appeared to be university students, while the remaining two were a couple in the middle of an argument. Chen Ge kept his attention on Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming, but as he collected the waivers, the female student unexpectedly called his name.

“You’re Chen Ge, the Haunted House boss that He San mentioned on the forum, right?”

Once Chen Ge’s name was mentioned, all the other visitors also turned to look at him.

“You know He San? Wait—are the three of you from Jiujiang Medical University’s forensic science department?” Chen Ge smoothly drew his attention away. The two suspected Ghost Stories Society members remained unaware that he had exposed them.

“He San is practically a celebrity at our school now.” The girl wore her hair in a single ponytail. She was slightly plump and very fair, not conventionally beautiful but undeniably charming. “Lots of students from our university have visited your Haunted House. There’s even a betting pool on the forum over which department will clear it first.”

“Clearing my Haunted House won’t be easy. You should ask He San for a few pointers.” Chen Ge broadened his smile until he looked as friendly as possible.

“It certainly isn’t. Six of us came, and half have already given up.” A frail-looking young man stood beside the girl. He plainly had feelings for her. Though his face was bloodless and his legs trembled, he had persisted in the hope of winning her affection.

“Why waste time? If we fail, we’ll try again. Repeat the same scenario often enough, and it won’t be scary anymore.” The third student stood on the girl’s other side and looked like the sort to charge headlong into any problem.

Chen Ge glanced at their names on the disclaimer and memorized them.

“You’ve already waited long enough, so I’ll keep this brief. Your goal is to find the name tags. Since there are only seven of you, finding seventeen will clear the scenario.” Chen Ge surveyed the group. “We’re also introducing a new feature. For an additional twenty, you may rent a costume and enter as a police officer, doctor, reporter, or another character.”

“We can wear costumes?” The girl brightened with interest, but the frail young man stopped her.

“It’s okay. The three of us won’t be trying it.”

“How about the rest of you?”

The couple remained absorbed in their argument and ignored him. The suspected Ghost Stories Society members showed no interest in dressing up either. Chen Ge was mildly disappointed; he had hoped they might test the new facility for him.

Chen Ge pulled aside the wooden boards and ushered the group underground. “Your scenario is Mu Yang High School, on the left. Do not take the wrong turn. The path on the right leads to our only three-star scenario, the Third Sick Hall. It is extremely dangerous. The last visitor who entered ended up in the hospital.”

Chen Ge mentioned the Third Sick Hall not out of kindness but to test the suspicious pair. If they were escaped patients, hearing the name should provoke some reaction. Every visitor nodded and promised not to wander, yet neither man’s expression changed. They did not seem aware that the Third Sick Hall existed here.

Was I mistaken?After offering a few final warnings, Chen Ge closed the boards and hurried to the control room. They may not be patients from the Third Sick Hall, but they are probably members of the Ghost Stories Society.

Chen Ge’s gaze remained calm, but his smile had vanished.Captain Yan found photographs of me entering New Century Park on Xu Tong’s phone. The Ghost Stories Society already knows what I look like.

The previous night, Xu Yin had consumed the monster possessing No. 5, and the police had arrested No. 12. Most importantly, Chen Ge had heard the chairperson’s voice through No. 12’s phone. Though the man had said little, that clue was the night’s greatest reward. I’ve heard the chairperson before. He must be someone I know—or at least someone I would recognize.

Each Ghost Stories Society member should have carried a possessing monster, making them strongest at night. Yet they had chosen to enter Chen Ge’s Haunted House during the day. Their unusual behavior suggested two possibilities.

First, exposing the chairperson’s voice mattered more than Chen Ge had realized. Afraid that Chen Ge might suddenly identify him, the man needed to silence him permanently before that happened.

Second, perhaps they feared Zhang Ya. Monsters were strongest after midnight and weakened during the day; Zhang Ya should be no exception.

But why choose today? They arrived just as the promotion began, so they must have planned this well in advance. They hoped to disappear among the crowds and avoid detection.

The Ghost Stories Society’s plan was sound; they were merely unlucky. They had not expected Wei Wu’s face to appear beside No. 5 in the surveillance image. Their infiltration had been exposed before it even began.

For now, I need to play along. There are too many visitors to disrupt the Haunted House’s operation.

The Ghost Stories Society had sent at least two members after the thin monster at Hai Ming Apartments. Given the importance they placed on Chen Ge, they would hardly send fewer against him.

Excluding me, the Ghost Stories Society has twelve members. Zhu Xiu, No. 5, and No. 12 have been dealt with, leaving nine.

Chen Ge entered the main control room and planted himself before the computer screens.

After today, there will only be seven left.

Chen Ge called Xiao Gu and told him to remove the Doctor Skull-cracker costume, then take the employees’ hidden passage to the control room.

“Have the visitors left?”

“They found the exit. I don’t think they were very afraid of me.” Xiao Gu sounded dejected. “I tried my best. Maybe I simply don’t have the talent for this.”

“Don’t give up so quickly.” Chen Ge donned the costume Gu Feiyu had removed. His lips twitched, drawing a ghastly smile across the skin mask. “Would you like to learn how to master this character?”

“Absolutely not.” Gu Feiyu shook his head with conviction. The moment Chen Ge put on Doctor Skull-cracker’s uniform, his entire presence changed, as though the costume had been made for him.

“Then we’ll help you develop an interest. Come with me.” Chen Ge seized Gu Feiyu by the shoulders and dragged him underground.

…

The wooden boards closed, cutting off the final ray of light. Darkness filled the underground scenario, and the visitors paused to let their eyes adjust.

“Everyone, remain calm. This scenario is difficult, but we still have a reasonable chance of clearing it.”

The student who had looked frail before Chen Ge transformed underground. His voice became steady and calm. Drawing a notebook from his pocket, he said, “Please give me thirty seconds. I need to review several precautions with everyone.”

“You brought notes to a Haunted House? What century are you living in? Haven’t you heard of phones?” the woman from the couple snapped, already in a foul mood.

“That brings me to my first point.” The young man indicated the first line in his notebook. “Never use your phone inside Boss Chen’s Haunted House. Ideally, don’t even touch it!”

He waved the notebook. “You may not believe me, but every detail here was learned through our seniors’ sweat and tears. Consider it a school tradition.”

“I think too much studying has driven you insane,” the woman said acidly. Her companion tugged at her sleeve. “Na Na, please. Don’t cause trouble.”

“Don’t touch me!” She slapped his hand away. “Chen Ziming, we first met in this Haunted House two years ago, so this is where we’ll break up. It’s time we went our separate ways. Goodbye!”

“Will you stop being so unreasonable? I haven’t had time for you because my career is at a critical stage. I can’t afford distractions right now!”

“So now I’m unreasonable? I’m a distraction? Do you think I care that much about your money?” The woman wore high heels and tasteful makeup. Her clothes were not expensive, but she carried them stylishly. “Chen Ziming, I stayed beside you at the lowest point of your life. I gave you two years!”

“I know, Na Na…”

“Save your breath. I know things are different now. Like this Haunted House, too much has changed in two years.” Having said her piece, the woman strode deeper into Mu Yang High School. The man hurried after her.

“Wait!” The frail-looking student clutched his notebook uneasily. “My second rule is never split up!”

He shouted after them, but the arguing couple paid no attention.

“Yang Chen, forget them. We can manage on our own.” The other two students from Jiujiang Medical University rallied around him.

“But clearing this scenario requires teamwork, and we were already disadvantaged by our small group.” Yang Chen sighed. “Now that only five of us remain, we absolutely cannot separate again.”

He turned to Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming. “Gentlemen, would you care to cooperate? We need seventeen name tags to clear the scenario.”

“Cooperate?” Wei Wu exchanged a glance with Kong Xiangming, but neither elaborated.

“You have no idea how devious this Haunted House’s boss is. If we don’t work together, our chance of clearing the scenario is zero.” Yang Chen unfolded a hand-drawn map from his notebook. Forty-one red crosses marked its surface.

“Consider this proof of our sincerity. Since Mu Yang High School opened, many senior students have challenged it. They found name tags in these forty-one places.” Yang Chen showed them the map. “The locations change, but a few spots consistently contain one. We should search all forty-one as quickly as possible.”

The map interested Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming, though clearing the scenario was the last thing on their minds.

“Sure, we’ll be glad for a chance to cooperate. After all, it benefits all of us.”

The two suspected Ghost Stories Society members agreed to collaborate with Yang Chen.

“We’re under a time limit, so I’ll divide the work.”

“Gentlemen, please search the classrooms on the left. Wang Dan, Li Xue, and I will take those on the right. Be careful. Keep your companions in sight, and if you must separate, stay in pairs.”

Yang Chen pocketed the map and regarded the others gravely. “Boss Chen’s Haunted House has several taboos: do not use your phone, do not wander off alone, and do not discuss marriage or relationships. Our seniors paid dearly for those conclusions. I don’t understand every warning, but each must exist for a reason. Remember them, and don’t test one merely out of curiosity.”

Yang Chen’s expression was serious, and his words confused Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming.

The team split to inspect opposite sides of the corridor. Once enough distance separated the groups, Wei Wu quietly moved beside Kong Xiangming. “This Haunted House makes me uneasy. Those taboos sound almost cursed.”

“Keep your distance. Remember, we aren’t supposed to know each other. There are cameras everywhere, so don’t let them catch us together.” Kong Xiangming pretended to search for name tags as he spoke.

“I still have a bad feeling.” Wei Wu searched as well, though his attention lay elsewhere.

“Stop talking and get to work. Don’t forget why we came.” Keeping his head lowered, Kong Xiangming’s eyes flashed with blood vessels. He glanced toward the entrance. “Boss Chen should arrive soon.”
